name: cart_items
title: Cart Items
description: One product in one basket, with the price it carried when it went in. Stamping the price at add-time is what lets the shop notice later that it moved: a price that changes while somebody is shopping must not silently change what they thought they were agreeing to, and a basket that has sat for three weeks must not hold the seller to a stale price either. Both numbers are kept and the DISAGREEMENT is surfaced at checkout (object_cart.price_changes) rather than resolved in secret in either direction -- the same instinct as stamping a rate at approval and refusing to let a later change restate it (docs/logic-decisions.md #1). No stock is reserved by anything here: availability is decided at checkout, because reserving on add is how a shop shows 'sold out' for goods nobody bought. A line also carries an INSTRUCTION and a price delta (line_note, modifier_cents), which is why the same product can appear on two lines of one basket: 'no onions' on the first burger and not the second are two different things to make. A large latte is genuinely its own product with its own SKU, price and stock, and variants-as-products already handles that; 'no onions' is not a product -- it has no SKU, it is an instruction on one line of one order, and modelling it as a product would put thousands of dead rows in the catalogue. 'Oat milk +60c' is the same instruction with a price delta, which is why the delta lives on the line rather than in the price book.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Description
fields.help: Stamped from the product name so a basket still reads correctly if the product is later renamed.

fields.name: quantity
fields.label: Quantity
fields.help: May be fractional -- 1.5 kg, 2.5 hours of setup -- so line money is Decimal arithmetic rounded once per line.

fields.name: unit_price_cents
fields.label: Unit Price
fields.help: What it cost when it went in the basket, in integer minor units. Compared against the live price at checkout, never quietly replaced by it.

fields.name: line_note
fields.label: Line Note
fields.help: What the shopper asked for on THIS line -- 'no onions', 'extra hot', 'cut in half'. An instruction, never a product: it has no SKU, it is true of one line of one order, and a catalogue row per instruction would be thousands of dead products. It is also never money: it reaches the kitchen ticket and the order line, and it changes no total anywhere.

fields.name: modifier_cents
fields.label: Modifier (cents)
fields.help: The price delta this instruction carries -- 'oat milk +60c' -- in integer minor units, PER UNIT, so two oat lattes cost two deltas. It lives on the line rather than in the price book for the same reason the note does: it is a fact about this order, not about the catalogue. Zero is the ordinary case. Never negative: a discount is a pricing decision that belongs in the price book or in a variant, and a shopper who can type their own negative delta can price their own lunch (action_cart refuses one).
